text:
incident-bot: :warning: Alerts: elevated 5xx rate and failed model cold-starts in eu-west-1a (5259876543)

emma_oncall: taking pager — seeing 5xx spike on hosted inference in eu-west-1a. p50 fine, p95 and p99 bad. tagging riley and zara.

pagerduty: Emma (emma_oncall) acknowledged the incident and is on-call.

riley_infra: looking at control-plane attach errors: kube events show `failed to assign network` for pod launches on g5 pool in eu-west-1a. aws sdk errors: ENIAllocationFailed/InsufficientIps.

zara_net: VPC-level view: subnet eu-w-1a-subnet-3 hitting IP exhaustion for free ENI secondary IPs. NLB target registrations are intermittently failing because new node interfaces can't attach. Also seeing resolver retries as services failover.

nora_prod: customer impact: batch inference jobs and some low-latency endpoints experiencing timeouts. We've got a few P1s from enterprise customers. CS alerted.

jan_support: customers reporting ~30s tail latencies and 503/504. Sharing sample request IDs.

riley_infra: this explains it. If the cluster can't attach ENIs, new pods can't join or get network, so LBs mark targets unhealthy. Old targets stick around but are under capacity -> 502s.

zara_net: quick mitigation: we can stop launching in that subnet and steer traffic to eu-west-1b/c. Also we can kick off a secondary subnet allocation in the same AZ if cloud provider permits on-the-fly.

emma_oncall: do the traffic shift now. Use weight-based reroute and also set out-of-az fallback for NLB health checks.

riley_infra: executing traffic-weight change: `rctl traffic-weight set inference.route=prod eu-west-1a=0.15 eu-west-1b=0.425 eu-west-1c=0.425`

incident-bot: :gear: Runbook step executed: traffic-weight update requested by riley_infra. jobId=9942

jan_support: FYI shifting will cause some cache misses. prepping prewarm for high-qps endpoints.

nora_prod: drafting customer note. keep it factual: "experiencing degraded performance in eu-west-1a, actively mitigating by shifting traffic." ETA for next update 20m.

zara_net: also flipping cluster networking fallback: `NET_ATTACH_MODE=secondary-subnet,prefer-cross-az` so new attachments try other subnets first.

riley_infra: applied weight change. Observing NLB healthy host count stabilize as new targets register in other AZs. p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 260ms. errors down to ~4%.

emma_oncall: good. But some long-lived connections to old targets are still failing intermittently (tcp rst). Can we force-drain the remaining targets in eu-west-1a?

riley_infra: initiating controlled drain: `infractl targetgroup drain --tg inference-g5-eu-west-1a --grace 120s`

zara_net: provider-side update: opened case with AWS. They confirm subnet IP exhaustion; they suggested either expand /24 to /23 (not trivial) or create a new ENI pool in a different subnet in the same AZ. They've queued a support change.

jan_support: CS flagged two customers who lost traffic for ~6 minutes during peak. sending immediate note and support ticket links.

nora_prod: update sent. included mitigation steps and ETA for next update.

riley_infra: to reduce blast radius for future, enabling aggressive ENI re-use for short-lived pods: `infra-config set eni.reuse=true eni.reuse_ttl=30s` — this reduces new IP churn. Applying now.

emma_oncall: do we want to spin up extra capacity in eu-west-1b/c Dedicated pools for SLA customers so they don't see degraded perf?

riley_infra: yes, scaling dedicated pool in eu-west-1b/c for critical customers: `dedicatectl scale --pool inference-prod-g5 --az eu-west-1b=+3 eu-west-1c=+3`

incident-bot: Job 9942 completed: weights applied.

zara_net: note: some clients cached the NLB IPs and still hit eu-west-1a for a few minutes. We're doing a distributed TTL flush on internal DNS and lowering external TTLs where possible.

emma_oncall: monitoring: p95 now ~240ms, errors 3.2%. marking incident state -> mitigating.

riley_infra: follow-up actions: 1) AWS change for extra subnet/ENI pool 2) replace or reprovision offending host groups if we see persistent attach errors 3) add ENI exhaustion alarms (free_ips < 10) per subnet 4) postmortem to analyze why autoscaler kept scheduling into exhausted subnet.

nora_prod: customers updated. scheduled detailed postmortem email for tomorrow.

jan_support: I'll take ongoing customer follow-ups.

pagerduty: Incident resolved by Emma (emma_oncall).

emma_oncall: closing pager but keeping thread open to capture timeline. quick snippets for incident doc: 
```
# detect ENI exhaustion
aws ec2 describe-subnets --subnet-ids SUBNET_ID | jq '.AvailableIpAddressCount'

# reroute traffic
rctl traffic-weight set inference.route=prod eu-west-1a=0.15 eu-west-1b=0.425 eu-west-1c=0.425

# drain targets
infractl targetgroup drain --tg inference-g5-eu-west-1a --grace 120s

# enable eni reuse
infra-config set eni.reuse=true eni.reuse_ttl=30s
```

zara_net: AWS update: scheduled pool change for today + guidance on subnet sizing. We'll track until fully remediated.

emma_oncall: plan: keep weights reduced for 60m, then ramp slowly once provider confirms ENI capacity or new subnet in place. postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC. thanks everyone. :pray:
